# rossark-motion-skill

rossark-motion-skill is a method for making drawn things feel alive without making them busy, from a production app's onboarding and paywall art where the brief was "it has to feel ALIVE" and "NO TELEPORTING in the animation". Its principles: never teleport, interpolate everything; calm by default with timed motion and strong curves, no bouncy overshoot unless the project explicitly wants a bouncy brand; small amplitudes, halving when unsure; arcs and pivots, with every moving part drawn as its own layer rotating around its pivot; overlap and follow-through, with phase delays growing along a chain; variety without chaos through seeded phases, speeds, and sizes, never Math.random per frame and never everything in sync; one main action per scene plus two or three idle loops; opacity only to appear or disappear; the layout never moves, motion happens inside the drawing; reduced motion means still, with loops frozen at frame 0 and one-shot scenes showing their final frame; nothing runs unseen, with clocks paused off screen, hidden, or in the background; and every move gets enough frames. The engine has one small motion core per platform: templates for React Native (react-native-svg plus Reanimated) and SwiftUI (TimelineView plus Canvas), with loop clocks, one-shot clocks, keyframe tracks, flow-through acting chains, and shaping helpers for waves, loops, bells, windows, and seeded variety. Recipes by subject give starting numbers for characters, tails, plants, cloth, fire, smoke...
